drawer.title: GEO readiness
drawer.subtitle: Can AI crawlers actually read this page?

verdict.ok: Every crawler we tested can read this page.
verdict.thin: Some crawlers receive far less text than a browser. The page may need JavaScript to show its content.
verdict.unpublished: This page has never been published, so there is no public URL to test yet.
verdict.empty: Even a browser receives almost no text before JavaScript runs ({{count}} words). Crawlers will see an empty page.
verdict.unreachable: The server could not reach the page for {{count}} crawler.
verdict.unreachable_plural: The server could not reach the page for {{count}} crawlers.

crawler.initialHtml: What the crawler receives before JavaScript runs

explain.403: The server refused this crawler. This is usually a firewall or bot-protection rule, not a content problem.
explain.jsOnly: A browser sees much more text than the crawler does. The content probably arrives through JavaScript, which crawlers do not run.
explain.empty: The initial HTML is a shell. The content arrives through JavaScript, or after a client-side redirect, and crawlers do not run either. Server-side rendering is the fix, not a robots.txt change.
explain.blockedButAllowed: Your robots.txt allows {{count}} of these crawlers, but the server refused them anyway. The block is coming from a firewall or bot protection, not from your content or your robots.txt. This is an infrastructure fix.
explain.reachableButDisallowed: Your robots.txt tells {{count}} of these crawlers not to fetch this page. They can reach it, but a well-behaved crawler will not read it. Change robots.txt if you want them to.

crawler.metaRefresh: Client-side redirect: the page tells a browser to go to {{url}}. Crawlers stay on this shell.

error.generic: The check could not be completed.
error.rateLimit: Too many checks in a short time. Try again in a few minutes.
error.notPublished: Publish this page first, then run the check.

robots.title: robots.txt
robots.absent: This site has no robots.txt. Every crawler is allowed everywhere by default. That works, but nobody decided it.
robots.noneNamed: No AI crawler is named in robots.txt. They all fall under the wildcard rule, so they are allowed by default rather than on purpose.
robots.someNamed: {{count}} AI crawler is named explicitly in robots.txt.
robots.someNamed_plural: {{count}} AI crawlers are named explicitly in robots.txt.
robots.someDisallowed: {{count}} of them cannot fetch this page.

control.title: Control AI crawlers
control.intro: Sets each crawler's site-wide stance in robots.txt. Groups you have not changed are left exactly as they are, comments and Sitemap lines included.
control.applied: Written and published. Run the check again to see it.
control.cannotWrite: You do not have permission to change this site's settings.
control.noMixin: This site has no robots.txt yet. Applying will create one.
control.placeholder: What is stored is the module's placeholder, not a real file.
control.error: robots.txt could not be read or written.
control.rule: Blocking replaces that crawler's rules with a site-wide refusal. Allowing only undoes a site-wide refusal: a crawler with path rules such as Disallow: /docs/ is left alone, because flattening that would throw away work. A crawler sharing a group with others is moved into its own group so the others keep their rules.
control.accessExplain: robots.txt states a policy. Only a fetch shows whether the server honours it.
control.verdictServed: All {{count}} AI crawlers are served by this site
control.verdictRefused: {{count}} AI crawler is refused by the server
control.verdictRefused_plural: {{count}} AI crawlers are refused by the server
control.verdictAgree: robots.txt and the server agree on every crawler.
control.verdictMismatch: {{count}} crawler is treated differently from what robots.txt says. One of the two is wrong.
control.verdictMismatch_plural: {{count}} crawlers are treated differently from what robots.txt says. One of the two is wrong.

bot.GPTBot: Collects pages to train OpenAI's models. Blocking it does not affect whether ChatGPT can cite you.
bot.OAI-SearchBot: Builds the index behind ChatGPT's search results. Blocking it takes you out of those answers.
bot.ChatGPT-User: Fetches a page when someone asks ChatGPT about it. Blocking it means ChatGPT cannot open your pages on request.
bot.ClaudeBot: Collects pages to train Anthropic's models. Blocking it does not affect whether Claude can cite you.
bot.Claude-SearchBot: Builds the index behind Claude's search. Blocking it takes you out of those answers.
bot.PerplexityBot: Builds Perplexity's search index. Blocking it takes you out of its answers.
bot.Perplexity-User: Fetches a page when someone asks Perplexity about it.
bot.Google-Extended: Controls whether your content trains Gemini and grounds its answers. It does not affect Google Search ranking.
bot.GoogleOther: A general-purpose Google crawler used by several product teams. Its exact use is not published.
bot.Bingbot: Builds the Bing index, which also grounds Microsoft Copilot. Blocking it takes you out of both.
bot.CCBot: Collects pages for Common Crawl, a public dataset many models train on.
bot.Bytespider: Collects pages to train ByteDance's models.
bot.Amazonbot: Crawls for Alexa answers and Amazon search.
bot.Applebot-Extended: Controls whether your content trains Apple Intelligence. It does not affect Siri or Spotlight results.
bot.meta-externalagent: Collects pages to train Meta's models.

control.searchBlockedTitle: {{count}} crawler that answers questions is blocked
control.searchBlockedTitle_plural: {{count}} crawlers that answer questions are blocked
control.searchBlocked: Blocking a crawler that builds answers removes you from that assistant's replies. Blocking one that only trains models does not. Check this is what you meant: {{names}}.
control.verdictUnreachable: The server could not reach the page for {{count}} crawler, so what the site does with it is unknown
control.verdictUnreachable_plural: The server could not reach the page for {{count}} crawlers, so what the site does with them is unknown

robots.unreachable: robots.txt could not be fetched, so what it allows is unknown. This is a connection problem, not a finding about the file.

llms.title: llms.txt
llms.absent: No llms.txt at the site root (HTTP {{status}}). AI engines have no curated map of your best content.
llms.servedHtml: The site returned an HTML page for /llms.txt instead of a text file. That counts as not having one.

stale.title: llms.txt links to pages that moved or were removed
stale.summary: {{count}} links of the file no longer lead to a published page. Fix them in Additional, SEO, Llms.txt.

why.addressChanged: the address changed, this one now redirects
why.gone: no longer published, or no visitor can read it

fresh.title: llms.txt links are up to date
fresh.summary: All {{count}} links to this site lead to a published page.

llms.unreachable: llms.txt could not be fetched, so whether the site publishes one is unknown. This is a connection problem, not a finding about the file.

view.title: llms.txt
view.intro: The llms.txt this site publishes, as the llms module serves it. It is written in that module's own screen; this tab shows it and checks that each of its links still leads to a published page.
view.empty: The llms module is enabled but no llms.txt is published yet. Write it in Additional, SEO, Llms.txt, then publish.
view.placeholder: What is published is the llms module's placeholder, not a real file. Write it in Additional, SEO, Llms.txt.
view.moduleOff: llms.txt is written and served by the llms module, which is not enabled on this site. Install it and enable it on the site to publish one.
view.error: The published llms.txt could not be read.

files.editedInSettings: robots.txt and llms.txt belong to the whole site. robots.txt is edited under Additional, SEO, GEO readiness; llms.txt under Additional, SEO, Llms.txt.

score.headline: {{passed}} of {{total}} checks passed
score.allGood: Everything we can check from here passes.
score.rubric: Each check reads one fact already in this report. Being disallowed in robots.txt is not counted as a failure: refusing a crawler is a legitimate choice. A disagreement between the policy and the server is.

reachable.label: Every AI crawler gets the page
reachable.fix: At least one crawler was refused. That is usually a firewall or bot-protection rule rather than a content problem.

policyMatchesReality.label: robots.txt matches what the server does
policyMatchesReality.fix: The policy and the server disagree for at least one crawler. One of the two is wrong, and the report names which.

noClientRedirect.label: No client-side redirect
noClientRedirect.fix: The page tells a browser to go elsewhere. Crawlers do not follow that, so this shell is all they read.

namedInRobots.label: AI crawlers named in robots.txt
namedInRobots.fix: No AI crawler is named. They fall to the wildcard group, so you have no explicit policy for them.

contentInInitialHtml.label: Real text in the initial HTML
contentInInitialHtml.fix: The page returns almost no text before JavaScript runs. Server-side rendering is the fix, not a robots.txt change.

sameContentForCrawlers.label: Crawlers get the same text as a browser
sameContentForCrawlers.fix: At least one crawler receives far less text than the browser did. Check what the server varies on the user agent.

title.label: Title present and a usable length
title.fix: A title under 10 or over 70 characters is either uninformative or truncated wherever it is quoted.

singleH1.label: Exactly one H1
singleH1.fix: Zero or several H1 headings leave the main subject of the page ambiguous.

headingOutline.label: Sub-headings structure the page
headingOutline.fix: Retrieval splits pages on headings. A page with no H2 is one undifferentiated block.

metaDescription.label: Meta description present
metaDescription.fix: Without it the summary shown alongside an answer is generated from whatever text comes first.

canonical.label: Canonical URL declared
canonical.fix: Without a canonical, the same content reachable at several addresses is treated as several pages.

langDeclared.label: Page language declared
langDeclared.fix: The html lang attribute is missing, so the language has to be guessed. On a multilingual site that is a real risk.

structuredData.label: Structured data present
structuredData.fix: No JSON-LD was found. Schema types are the most direct way to state what this page is about.

freshness.label: Modification date published
freshness.fix: No dateModified was found. Assistants weigh recency, and an undated page cannot show it is current.

imageAlt.label: Images carry alt text
imageAlt.fix: Some images have no alt text. To a text-only crawler those images simply do not exist.

robotsPresent.label: robots.txt is served
robotsPresent.fix: No robots.txt. Everything is allowed by default, which is a decision you did not get to make.

llmsPresent.label: llms.txt is served
llmsPresent.fix: No llms.txt. It is the one file that tells an assistant which pages matter and why.

guestReadable.label: A visitor with no account can read it
guestReadable.fix: A guest cannot read this page, so no crawler ever will. Some servers answer a gated page with a login form and a 200, which looks like success. Check the page's access restrictions.

fetched.label: The server could fetch the page
fetched.fix: The server could not connect to the page for at least one crawler. This is a connection problem on the server, not a refusal by the site, and the checks of what arrives are unreliable until it is fixed.

score.fromTemplate: Comes from the template “{{template}}”, which renders {{count}} pages. Fixing it there fixes all of them.

diff.identical: No change. The file would be written exactly as it is now.

dashboard.title: GEO readiness for site {{site}} - {{language}}
dashboard.intro: robots.txt states the policy for AI crawlers and is edited here. llms.txt says which pages matter and why: it is written in the llms module and shown here read only. Both belong to the whole site, not to a page.

visibility.title: Content no AI can read
visibility.intro: Published pages that a visitor with no account cannot read. A crawler served a login form gets a cheerful 200 and reports success, so only the repository knows these pages are invisible.
visibility.summary: {{readable}} of {{scanned}} published pages can be read by a visitor with no account
visibility.noFindings: Every published page can be read without an account.
visibility.truncated: Only the first {{scanned}} pages were scanned. The rest were not looked at.
visibility.deliberateIntro: Pages inside a branch that is closed as a whole, which normally means a members area rather than a mistake.
visibility.error: The scan could not be completed.

kind.hiddenByCondition: Hidden right now by a visibility condition
kind.noindex: Set to noindex, so it will not be cited

visibility.noindexTitle: This page is set to noindex
visibility.noindex: Search engines and AI crawlers are told not to index this page, so it will not be cited. That is often deliberate for legal or utility pages. If it is not, the setting is on the page itself.
visibility.gatedTitle: No visitor can read this page
visibility.gated: A visitor with no account cannot open this page, so no AI crawler ever will. Some servers answer a gated page with a login form and a 200, which looks like success from outside. The setting is in the page's access restrictions.

score17.title: Site score
score17.intro: Every published page scored, one fetch each, on a schedule you set. The per-page drawer fetches as sixteen crawlers to compare them; doing that site-wide would be hundreds of thousands of requests, so a scan fetches once per page as a single AI crawler.
score17.headline: {{percent}}% of checks pass across the site
score17.up: up {{n}} points since the last run
score17.down: down {{n}} points since the last run
score17.counts: {{scored}} pages scored · {{critical}} with a critical failure · {{unreadable}} no visitor can read
score17.failed: The run did not finish. The server log has the detail.
score17.scheduleHelp: A Quartz cron expression, in the server's timezone. Leave the scope empty to scan the whole site, or give a path to scan one branch. A running scan appears in the administration job list.
score17.badCron: That is not a cron expression Quartz accepts. Nothing was saved.
score17.rateLimit: Too many scans in a short time. Try again in a few minutes.
score17.error: The scan state could not be read.
score17.truncated: The scan stopped at {{pages}} pages. Narrow the scope, or raise the limit.
score17.enabledHelp: When off, the site is only scanned when you press Scan now.
score17.cronHelp: Runs in the server's timezone, not your browser's.
score17.scopeHelp: Leave empty for the whole site, or choose a branch to scan only that part.
score17.whyFewer: 17 checks here, 18 in the page drawer. Comparing what a crawler receives against what a browser receives needs a second fetch of the same page, so “{{check}}” is only evaluated one page at a time. Both counts report the same failures.
score17.byTemplateHelp: A check is blamed on the template only when it fails on nearly every page that template renders. Three pages failing out of four hundred is three authors; four hundred out of four hundred is the template.
score17.templateClean: Nothing here is the template's fault.
score17.matrixHelp: One cell per page and check. A column that is solid top to bottom is the template's doing, not the authors'.

sitemap.title: Sitemap against reality
sitemap.agrees: All {{entries}} entries resolve to published content, and nothing published is missing from it.
sitemap.notListedTitle: This page is not in the sitemap
sitemap.notListed: The site publishes a sitemap and this page is not in it, so a crawler has no reason to look for it.

kind.missing: Published, but not in the sitemap
kind.unknown: In the sitemap, but nothing published answers
kind.staleDate: The date in the sitemap is wrong
kind.noindexListed: Listed in the sitemap and marked noindex
kind.redirects: The sitemap lists an address that redirects

why.missing: A crawler has no reason to look for these.
why.unknown: Crawl budget spent on addresses that lead nowhere.
why.staleDate: Claiming a page is older than it is tells crawlers not to bother recrawling it. Shown as claimed then actual.
why.noindexListed: The map says index this, the page says do not. One of the two is a mistake.
why.redirects: These pages have a vanity URL, and the sitemap still names the address Jahia redirects away from. Crawlers are being sent through a redirect to reach content that has a direct address, and search engines want the final URL in a sitemap.

sitemap.counts: {{entries}} entries in the sitemap · {{published}} published pages and content items a visitor can read.
sitemap.noindexListedTitle: This page is in the sitemap and marked noindex
sitemap.noindexListedPage: The sitemap tells crawlers to index this page and the page itself tells them not to. One of the two is a mistake.
sitemap.staleTitle: The sitemap's date for this page is wrong
sitemap.stalePage: The sitemap claims {{detail}}. A crawler that trusts the earlier date has no reason to come back for what changed.
sitemap.intro: What the sitemap says against what the site actually publishes. Entries are resolved against the repository rather than fetched, so this costs no requests and needs no site scan. The scheduled scan refreshes it too.
sitemap.never: Run a check, or wait for the next scheduled site scan, which refreshes this too.
sitemap.limits: Entries are matched to content, not fetched, so a redirect is not detected: an entry that redirects elsewhere counts as resolving. Every language of the site is compared, and each finding names the URL it belongs to.

error.failed: The sitemap could not be read or compared. The server log has the detail.
error.rate: Wait a moment before checking again.

absent.none: Nothing answers {{url}} (HTTP {{status}}), so crawlers are handed no map of this site at all. The Sitemap module publishes one per site.
absent.notSitemapTitle: That address answers, but not with a sitemap
absent.notSitemap: {{url}} returns HTTP {{status}}, but the response is not a sitemap - most often a page or an error page served with a success code. Until that address returns a real sitemap, crawlers have no usable map, and nothing here can be compared.
absent.unreachableTitle: The sitemap could not be reached
absent.unreachable: {{url}} could not be fetched at all, so whether a sitemap exists is unknown. This is a connection problem, not a finding about your content.

sitemap.unreachablePageTitle: The last site scan could not reach the sitemap
sitemap.unreachablePage: {{url}} could not be fetched during the site scan of {{date}}, so whether this page is in the sitemap is unknown.

links.title: Pages nothing links to
links.intro: A crawler can tell you what it found. It cannot tell you what it missed, because it never knew the page existed. This compares everything published against everything the site actually links to, using the rendered HTML of each page the last scan fetched.
links.counts: {{pages}} published pages judged, from {{read}} pages read in this language.
links.never: The link graph is built from the rendered HTML of every page, so it comes from a site scan. Run one from the Site score tab.
links.allLinkedTitle: Every page is linked from somewhere
links.allLinked: No published page in this language is unreachable, and none depends on the menus alone.

kind.orphans: Nothing links here, and the sitemap does not list it
kind.weak: Reachable, but nobody chose to link it

why.orphans: No page links to these and no sitemap entry names them. Nothing will ever find them.
why.weak: A crawler can reach these, but only through a menu that lists everything or through the sitemap. No author linked to them, and link-weighted crawlers treat that as a weak signal.

links.limits: Links are read from rendered HTML, so a menu built from the page tree, a listing, a rich text link and a configured button all count the same. One link per source page: linking twice from the same page is one decision. Only the language of this scan is judged, since only its pages were fetched. Your home page is never reported.
links.orphanPage: No other published page links here and the sitemap does not list it, so a crawler has no way to discover it at all.
links.navOnlyTitle: Only the menu links to this page
links.navOnlyPage: It appears in navigation on {{count}} pages, but no page links to it from its content. Crawlers that weight links treat a menu entry as a weaker signal than a link an author chose to make.

vanity.title: One page, several addresses
vanity.intro: Jahia owns the vanity URL service, so every address a page answers on is a repository fact rather than something to be discovered by crawling. This is that list, checked against the languages the site serves and against what each page says its canonical is.
vanity.never: The canonical half of this check reads the rendered pages, so it comes from a site scan. Run one from the Site score tab.
vanity.noneTitle: This site uses no vanity URLs
vanity.none: Every page answers on its own address only, so nothing here can be split across duplicates.
vanity.agrees: All {{total}} vanity URLs resolve, none competes with another, and the pages say which address counts.

kind.unresolvable: Registered under a language this site does not serve

why.unresolvable: These cannot resolve. The language they are filed under is not one this site publishes, so the address returns a 404 to everybody, including crawlers that were told about it.
why.duplicates: The same content answers on more than one address in the same language. Anything counting links now has two places to put the credit.
why.canonical: The page carries no canonical tag, or one pointing somewhere that is neither its own address nor any of its aliases.

vanity.limits: Inactive vanity URLs are ignored: switching one off is a decision, not a fault. Two pages cannot claim the same address - Jahia renames the second on save, which is where the -1 suffixes on imported sites come from - so there is deliberately no check for it. The canonical part covers only pages the last scan fetched.

page.unresolvableTitle: This page has an address that cannot work
page.unresolvable: A vanity URL is filed under the language "{{detail}}", which this site does not serve, so that address returns a 404 to everybody.
page.duplicateTitle: This page answers on several addresses
page.duplicate: It is reachable at {{detail}}. One is marked default, so engines have a hint, but every link to the other still splits the signal.
page.noDefaultTitle: This page answers on several addresses and none is the default
page.noDefault: It is reachable at {{detail}}, and nothing marks which one is real. Set one as the default vanity URL.
page.missingTitle: This page has aliases but no canonical tag
page.missing: It answers on more than one address and the page does not say which one counts, so engines have to guess.
page.elsewhereTitle: This page's canonical points somewhere unexpected
page.elsewhere: The canonical names {{detail}}, which is neither this page's own address nor any of its vanity URLs. Everything this page earns is being credited elsewhere.
page.canonical: The canonical tag does not name this page's own address or any of its aliases.

freshness.title: Where the site has gone stale
freshness.intro: How old everything a visitor can read actually is, taken from the repository rather than from the dates pages choose to publish. Grouped rather than ranked: a legal notice and a property listing age for different reasons, and a single list of oldest-first would put them side by side.
freshness.counts: {{total}} published items dated, {{undated}} with no modification date.
freshness.thresholdLabel: Flag a group when nothing in it has changed in
freshness.never: Pick a threshold above to age the published content. It is a repository query, so it answers straight away.
freshness.byTypeHelp: How long since anything of this kind changed at all. Longer is worse, and the distinction is what stops a legal page being flagged next to a news article.
freshness.bySectionHelp: The same measure, grouped the way the work is usually divided up.
freshness.limits: A group is flagged on its newest item, not its oldest or its average: "nothing here has been touched" is actionable, while "the oldest item is old" is true of every site. Dates are the repository's own, so a page rebuilt without content changes does not count as fresh. Only the language shown is measured, since a translation carries its own dates.
freshness.whenTitle: When the site was last touched
freshness.allHelp: The whole list, so the groups above tell you where to look and this tells you which page. Each row opens in jContent.
freshness.truncated: Long lists are cut at {{count}} rows; the groups above still count everything.

languages.title: Readiness one language at a time
languages.intro: A single figure for the whole site hides the market that is failing. This is coverage and score for each language the site declares, side by side, so a strong language cannot average out a weak one.
languages.counts: {{total}} published items, {{count}} languages declared by this site.
languages.unmeasuredTitle: Some languages have never been scanned
languages.unmeasured: {{count}} of these languages has no score yet, which is not the same as scoring badly. A scan runs one language at a time, so each one needs its own schedule on the Site score tab.
languages.spreadTitle: One market is measurably behind another
languages.spread: There are {{points}} points between the best and worst language. An average across the site would have hidden that, which is exactly how a market ends up invisible to assistants while the brand looks healthy overall.
languages.errorTitle: Language coverage could not be read
languages.error: The repository could not be queried for translations. The server log has the detail.
languages.limits: Coverage counts pages and content items that carry a translation, whether or not anyone has written into it; an empty translation counts as present. Scores come from whatever scan last ran in that language, so two languages scanned weeks apart are not measured against the same site.
languages.pageMissingTitle: This page does not exist in every language
languages.pageMissing: It has no translation in: {{languages}}. Assistants answering in those languages have nothing of this page to cite.
languages.pageUnpublishedTitle: A translation of this page is not published
languages.pageUnpublished: It is translated into {{languages}} but that translation has not been published, so no visitor or crawler can see it.

schema.none: No structured data was generated for this page.
schema.headline: schema.org {{type}}
schema.complete: everything it needs has a source in the content model
schema.unmappedTitle: This content type is not mapped yet
schema.unmapped: Nothing says what a {{nodeType}} is in schema.org terms, so no structured data can be derived from it.
schema.unmappedHelp: Map it on the Structured data tab of the GEO readiness dashboard. Nothing guesses here: a type is whatever the person who defined it says it is.
schema.conflict: The generated {{property}} is "{{generated}}" while the page displays "{{page}}". Structured data that disagrees with the visible content is worse than none, so fix one of the two before using this.
schema.missing: The content model has nothing to fill: {{properties}}. They are left out rather than invented, because a value that is not in the content is a value the page does not support.
schema.limits: Generated from the content type, not written into the page. Paste it into the template for this type so every item gets it, rather than into one page. Values are read from the published content in this language.

panel.title: Structured data from the content model
panel.intro: Every other tool infers schema.org output from the words on a page. The content type already says what the content is, so it can be derived instead - which is both cheaper and more accurate. Map each type once and every item of it can emit correct JSON-LD.
panel.counts: {{mapped}} of {{total}} published items have a mapped type, {{complete}} of them can fill everything their schema type requires.
panel.readyType: every required property has a source
panel.thin: Recommended but unavailable: {{properties}}. Valid without them, richer with them.
panel.errorTitle: The content model could not be read
panel.error: Node types could not be listed for this site. The server log has the detail.
panel.limits: Saving a mapping stores it. It never writes into a page or a template: the drawer shows the snippet for a page and a person places it. "Deliberately none" marks a type that should not emit structured data, so it stops being reported as unmapped.

legend.incomplete: Mapped, but a required property has no source

panel.suggested: From the properties it holds, {{type}} describes this model better.

context.links: {{nav}} pages link here from navigation, {{content}} from page content

report.title: The written report
report.intro: Everything else on this dashboard is measured and says so. This tab asks a model to read those measurements and write what they add up to: where the site stands for AI crawlers, what to fix first, who can fix it, and in what order. It answers only when you ask, because each answer is paid for and takes a while.
report.notConfigured: Set AI_PROVIDER, AI_MODEL and AI_API_KEY in digital-factory-data/karaf/etc/org.jahia.community.contentgovernance.llm.cfg to enable this tab. Nothing leaves the server until then.
report.privacy: The provider receives this site's measurements: scores, failing check ids, page paths and titles, counts. Never page bodies, never the key.
report.generatingHint: Reading the measurements and writing. This can take up to a minute.
report.never: Run a site scan first so there is something to read, then ask for the report. The sitemap, links, freshness and language panels feed it too.
report.errorTitle: The report could not be written
report.rateLimited: Too many reports asked for in ten minutes. The limit protects the budget; try again shortly.
report.otherLanguage: This report was written in {{have}}. Your interface is in {{want}}: write it again to get it in your language.
report.truncated: The model ran out of room before finishing. The end of the report may be missing; raising AI_REPORT_MAX_TOKENS gives it more.
report.none: Nothing to recommend: the measurements gave the model nothing to act on.
report.disclaimer: Written by a model from measurements this module took. It prioritises and explains; it does not measure anything itself, and it can be wrong. Check a recommendation against the panel it refers to before acting on it.
report.notConfiguredTab: No AI provider is configured on this server.

fetchError.ConnectException: The server could not open a connection to that address ({{error}}). A Jahia Cloud server, for one, cannot reach its own public address: ask for that to be allowed, or set PUBLIC_BASE_URL to an address the server can reach.
fetchError.SocketTimeoutException: The address did not answer in time ({{error}}).
fetchError.SSLHandshakeException: The server's Java does not trust the certificate of that address ({{error}}).
fetchError.UnknownHostException: The server cannot resolve that host name ({{error}}).

citations.asOfUnknown: BotRank has not counted any AI answer yet.
citations.notSynced: The site is connected to BotRank, but its first sync has not run. Figures appear after the next daily sync, or after a site administrator starts one.
citations.notPublished: AI answers can only cite a published page. Publish it, and its citations appear after the next sync.

eco.disclaimer: Page-level checks against the RGESN 2024 Frontend/Contents families. This is not an RGESN conformity score - a full assessment covers the whole service (hosting, backend, governance); see the manual checklist below. Resource figures are from the editing-workspace render and are indicative.

pageWeight.title: Heavy page ({{size}})
pageWeight.detail: Compress images, drop unused scripts/styles and defer non-critical resources. A lighter page consumes less energy and bandwidth per visit (RGESN Frontend).

requests.title: {{count}} HTTP requests
requests.detail: Each request costs a round-trip and server work. Combine assets, lazy-load below-the-fold content and remove unused third-party scripts (RGESN Frontend).

domSize.title: Large DOM ({{count}} nodes)
domSize.detail: A heavy DOM increases memory use and rendering energy on the visitor's device. Simplify the markup or paginate very long pages (RGESN Frontend).

lazyLoading.title: {{count}} below-the-fold images load eagerly
lazyLoading.detail: Add loading="lazy" so off-screen images are only fetched if the visitor scrolls to them - avoids downloading data that is never seen (RGESN Frontend).

imageFormats.title: {{count}} heavy images in legacy formats
imageFormats.detail: Serve WebP or AVIF instead of JPEG/PNG for a large size reduction at equal quality; let Jahia generate modern-format renditions (RGESN Contents).

oversizedImages.title: {{count}} images larger than displayed
oversizedImages.detail: The source file is much bigger than its rendered size. Upload resized variants or use responsive renditions so no wasted pixels are transferred (RGESN Contents).

imageDimensions.title: {{count}} images without width/height
imageDimensions.detail: Explicit dimensions avoid re-layouts (and the extra rendering work they cost) as images load (RGESN Contents).

webFonts.title: {{count}} web font files loaded
webFonts.detail: Each font file is an extra download. Prefer system fonts, limit weights/styles, and use WOFF2 only (RGESN Frontend).

autoplay.title: {{count}} media elements autoplay
autoplay.detail: Autoplaying video/audio consumes bandwidth and battery before any interaction. Require an explicit play action (RGESN UX/UI).

thirdParty.title: {{count}} third-party origins
thirdParty.detail: Each external origin adds DNS/TLS connections, energy and privacy exposure. Self-host or remove non-essential third parties (RGESN Architecture).

checklist.title: Manual checklist (whole-service, not automatable)
checklist.intro: These RGESN criteria are assessed at the service level and cannot be judged from a single page. Review them with the team responsible for the platform.

envTarget.title: Environmental targets are defined and owned
envTarget.detail: The service has documented eco-design objectives and a person accountable for them (RGESN Strategy).

reviewMissing.title: Environmental impact is measured and reviewed
reviewMissing.detail: Impact indicators are tracked over releases, not set once and forgotten (RGESN Strategy).

greenHost.title: Low-carbon hosting
greenHost.detail: The infrastructure runs on a provider with a documented low PUE and renewable-energy commitment (RGESN Hosting).

caching.title: Effective caching of static resources
caching.detail: Long-lived cache headers and a CDN avoid re-downloading unchanged assets on every visit (RGESN Hosting/Architecture).

apiEfficiency.title: APIs return only what is needed
apiEfficiency.detail: Endpoints avoid over-fetching; payloads are paginated and scoped to the fields actually used (RGESN Backend).

pagination.title: Pagination over infinite scroll for large lists
pagination.detail: Infinite scroll keeps loading data the visitor may never read; paginate or lazy-load on demand (RGESN Backend/UX).

featureNeed.title: Every feature earns its footprint
featureNeed.detail: Features are justified against user need; unused ones are removed rather than shipped and maintained (RGESN UX).

noDarkPattern.title: No engagement dark patterns
noDarkPattern.detail: Autoplay carousels, aggressive notifications and endless feeds drive needless traffic and energy - avoid them (RGESN UX).

rawI18nKeys.detail: Text like namespace:key.path means a resource bundle or locale JSON entry is missing: visitors see the technical key instead of the label. Usually a module i18n gap.

unpublishedChanges.detail: These nodes were modified or never published: visitors currently see an older version of this page, or nothing at all. Publish the page to align live with what you are editing.

missingTranslations.title: {{count}} content blocks missing translations ({{languages}})
missingTranslations.detail: This content renders empty or falls back to another language for visitors browsing in those languages. Open each node in the editor and fill in the missing languages.

placeholderText.title: {{count}} placeholder texts on the page
placeholderText.detail: Lorem ipsum / TODO text is still visible. Replace it with final content before publishing.

graphqlUnavailable.title: Repository checks could not run
graphqlUnavailable.detail: The GraphQL query failed, so publication and translation checks were skipped. The on-page checks above remain valid.

seo.noPreview: No title or og:title found - nothing to preview.
seo.noOgImage: No og:image - shared links will have no visual

assist.title: AI suggestions
assist.intro: Ready-to-paste title, meta description, keyword and heading suggestions, written in the page language ({{language}}) by {{provider}} from what the page actually says. Copy them into the page's SEO properties or the heading content - nothing is changed automatically.
assist.generating: Writing suggestions… this takes a few seconds.
assist.socialHint: og:title and og:description for the sharing card on social networks and chat tools - fill them in the page's social/SEO properties.
assist.keywordsHint: Focus keyword (dark) and supporting terms to weave into headings and copy. Search engines ignore the meta keywords tag - use these to guide the writing, not as a tag.
assist.ctasHint: Generic labels ("Read more", "Click here", "Submit") tell visitors and search engines nothing. Pick a specific label and set it on the link or button in Content Editor.
assist.headingsHint: Headings are page content: edit the heading component in Content Editor, not the SEO properties.
assist.missingHeading: No h1 on the page - proposed:

noTitle.title: The page has no title
noTitle.detail: The <title> is the strongest on-page SEO signal and the text shown in search results. Set one in the page's SEO properties.

titleLength.title: Title is {{length}} characters
titleLength.detail: Aim for {{min}}-{{max}} characters: shorter wastes the space, longer gets truncated in search results.

noDescription.title: No meta description
noDescription.detail: Search engines will pick an arbitrary text snippet. Write a 50-160 character summary that makes people want to click.

descriptionLength.title: Meta description is {{length}} characters
descriptionLength.detail: Aim for {{min}}-{{max}} characters so the full text shows in search results.

noindex.title: Page is excluded from search engines (noindex)
noindex.detail: The robots meta tag contains noindex ({{content}}). If this page should be public, remove it - it will never appear in search results.

nofollow.title: Links are not followed (nofollow)
nofollow.detail: The robots meta tag contains nofollow ({{content}}): search engines ignore every link on this page. Verify it is intentional.

noCanonical.title: No canonical URL
noCanonical.detail: A canonical link prevents duplicate-content issues when the page is reachable through several URLs (vanity URLs, parameters).

incompleteOg.title: Incomplete Open Graph tags
incompleteOg.detail: Without og:title and og:image, links shared on social networks and chat tools render as bare URLs. Fill in the page's social/SEO properties.

invalidStructuredData.title: {{count}} invalid JSON-LD blocks
invalidStructuredData.detail: The structured data does not parse, so search engines ignore it. Validate the JSON-LD markup.

noStructuredData.title: No structured data
noStructuredData.detail: JSON-LD (Article, Organization, BreadcrumbList…) enables rich results in search engines. Worth adding on key pages.

noLang.title: Missing lang attribute on <html>
noLang.detail: Screen readers and search engines cannot tell what language the page is in. The template should set <html lang>.

langMismatch.title: Page declares lang="{{htmlLang}}" but is audited in "{{expected}}"
langMismatch.detail: A wrong lang attribute confuses search engines and screen reader pronunciation. Check the template's language handling.

missingAlt.title: {{count}} images without alt attribute
missingAlt.detail: Alt text is how search engines and screen readers understand images. Fill the alt field on each image in the content editor.

genericAnchors.title: {{count}} generic link texts ("click here", "read more"…)
genericAnchors.detail: Descriptive link text helps SEO and screen reader users. Say where the link goes: "Read the 2026 annual report".

links.externalNote: external links are not verified (browser cross-origin restriction)

brokenLinks.title: {{count}} broken internal links
brokenLinks.detail: These links return an error for visitors. Fix or remove them - the list below shows each one with a highlight button.

hardcodedUrls.title: {{count}} absolute URLs hardcoded to this host
hardcodedUrls.detail: Links written with the full http(s)://host break when the site moves environment or domain. Use internal page links instead.

mixedContent.title: {{count}} http:// links on an https page
mixedContent.detail: Browsers flag or block mixed content. Switch these URLs to https.

blankNoopener.title: {{count}} target="_blank" links without rel="noopener"
blankNoopener.detail: Pages opened in a new tab get access to this page's window object. Add rel="noopener" in the template or rich-text content.

recs.title: Recommendations
recs.none: Nothing to improve in this category.

alt.title: AI alt text
alt.intro: {{count}} image(s) have no alt attribute. Suggest alternative text written in the page language ({{language}}) from the picture and its context, then paste it into the image's alt field in Content Editor. Purely decorative images are identified so you can give them an empty alt.
alt.generating: Describing the images… this takes a few seconds.
alt.noVision: Note: {{provider}} does not process images - suggestions are inferred from file names and surrounding text only. Anthropic and OpenAI models see the actual picture.
alt.noAnswer: No suggestion returned for this image.
alt.more: {{count}} more image(s) without alt were not sent (8 per request) - fix these first, re-run the audit and suggest again.

a11y.noViolations: No violations detected by automated checks.
a11y.machineNote: Automated checks cover a subset of WCAG criteria. A clean result does not certify full compliance; the manual checklist below covers the rest.
a11y.incompleteNote: The engine suspects an issue here but cannot decide automatically - review each case.

checklist.title: Manual checklist (not automatable)
checklist.intro: These WCAG criteria require human judgment - no tool can verify them. Review them once per page type or template.

keyboard.title: Everything operable with the keyboard alone
keyboard.detail: Tab / Shift+Tab through the page: every menu, carousel, accordion and dialog must be reachable and usable, with no focus trap (WCAG 2.1.1, 2.1.2).

altQuality.title: Alt texts are meaningful
altQuality.detail: The tool checks that alt exists - only you can judge if it describes the image. Decorative images should have an empty alt (WCAG 1.1.1).

media.title: Videos have captions, audio has transcripts
media.detail: And the captions are accurate, not just auto-generated noise (WCAG 1.2.1-1.2.3).

focusOrder.title: Focus and reading order match the visual order
focusOrder.detail: Tab through the page: the focus must move in the order a sighted reader would scan it (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).

linkPurpose.title: Every link makes sense out of context
linkPurpose.detail: A screen reader user often lists all links: each label alone must say where it leads (WCAG 2.4.4).

zoom.title: Page usable at 200% zoom
zoom.detail: Ctrl/Cmd + until 200%: no text loss, no overlapping content (WCAG 1.4.4).

reflow.title: Content reflows at 320 px width
reflow.detail: Narrow the window (or use the mobile preview): no horizontal scrolling of the page body (WCAG 1.4.10).

focusVisible.title: Keyboard focus is always visible
focusVisible.detail: While tabbing, you must always see where you are - no invisible focus states (WCAG 2.4.7).

formErrors.title: Form errors are explained and fixable
formErrors.detail: Errors are identified in text (not color alone) and suggest a correction (WCAG 3.3.1, 3.3.3).

consistency.title: Navigation and components consistent across pages
consistency.detail: Menus, search, breadcrumbs appear in the same place and behave the same on every page (WCAG 3.2.3, 3.2.4).

readingLevel.title: Text understandable at lower-secondary reading level
readingLevel.detail: Use the Readability tab as a proxy, then judge jargon and sentence complexity yourself (WCAG 3.1.5).

timing.title: No time limits, or they can be turned off
timing.detail: Sessions, carousels or forms must not expire without warning and control (WCAG 2.2.3).

targetSize.title: Touch targets at least 44×44 px
targetSize.detail: Buttons and links comfortably tappable on mobile, with spacing between them (WCAG 2.5.5).

contextHelp.title: Context-sensitive help available
contextHelp.detail: Complex forms offer inline help or instructions where the user needs them (WCAG 3.3.5).

vitals.labNote: Lab measurement of this preview render. Values are directional and differ from real-user (field) data.

slowLcp.title: Main content renders slowly
slowLcp.detail: Compress or preload the hero image / largest block so visitors see the main content sooner.

highCls.title: Layout shifts while loading
highCls.detail: Reserve space for images, embeds and late-loading blocks so the page does not jump under the reader.

slowTtfb.title: Slow server response (TTFB)
slowTtfb.detail: The HTML itself is slow to arrive: enable page caching or review server load before optimizing anything else.

missingDims.title: {{count}} images without width/height attributes
missingDims.detail: Add width and height so the browser reserves the space up front - this is the most common cause of layout shifts.

oversizedImages.title: {{count}} images heavier than needed
oversizedImages.detail: The source file is more than twice its displayed size. Upload resized variants or let Jahia serve smaller renditions.

heavyPage.title: Heavy page ({{size}})
heavyPage.detail: Compress images and remove unused scripts/styles to reduce total download weight, especially for mobile visitors.

manyRequests.title: {{count}} network requests
manyRequests.detail: Combine or drop resources and lazy-load below-the-fold content: each request adds latency.

largeDom.title: Large DOM ({{count}} nodes)
largeDom.detail: Simplify the markup or split very long pages: a large DOM slows rendering and every interaction.

heavyAssets.title: {{count}} very large files (e.g. {{name}})
heavyAssets.detail: Minify, compress or split these assets, or load them only where actually used.

simplify.title: AI plain-language rewrites
simplify.intro: The score penalizes long sentences ({{count}} over 25 words). Rewrite up to 6 of the hardest paragraph sentences in plain language ({{language}}) - same facts, shorter sentences, common words - then paste the rewrite over the original in Content Editor.
simplify.generating: Rewriting… this takes a few seconds.
simplify.noAnswer: No rewrite returned for this sentence.
simplify.more: {{count}} more long sentence(s) were not sent (6 per request) - fix these first, re-run the audit and rewrite again.

readability.h1Hint: a page should have exactly one H1
readability.headingSkipsHint: avoid jumping levels (e.g. H2 to H4)
readability.noText: Not enough text on this page to compute readability ({{count}} words found).

veryHardText.title: Text is very difficult to read (score {{score}})
veryHardText.detail: Shorten sentences and prefer everyday words. Aim for a score above 50 for a general audience.

hardText.title: Text is difficult to read (score {{score}})
hardText.detail: Shorten the longest sentences and replace jargon: a score of 50-70 suits most website visitors.

longSentences.title: {{count}} sentences longer than 25 words
longSentences.detail: Split them - one idea per sentence. Long sentences are the main driver of a poor readability score.

longParagraphs.title: Dense paragraphs ({{count}} words on average)
longParagraphs.detail: Break paragraphs up: 40-60 words per paragraph reads comfortably on screen.

h1Count.title: {{count}} H1 headings on the page
h1Count.detail: Use exactly one H1: it anchors the page for readers, screen readers and search engines.

headingSkips.title: {{count}} skipped heading levels
headingSkips.detail: Do not jump levels (e.g. H2 straight to H4): fix the hierarchy so the document outline stays meaningful.

thinContent.title: Little text on the page ({{count}} words)
thinContent.detail: Pages under ~300 words inform and rank poorly. Consider expanding the content or merging it elsewhere.

drawer.title: Content governance

drawer.nothingAvailable: No section of Content governance can be used on this content.

sectionHelp.audit: Checks the page you are editing: accessibility, SEO, speed, readability, eco-design, links and Jahia content, with AI suggestions on demand.
sectionHelp.geo: Whether AI assistants and their crawlers can read and cite the published page: score, crawler access, site files, structured data and AI citations.
sectionHelp.compliance: Terms from the site glossaries that this page, and the content it shows, must not use in this language.

settings.title: Content governance
settings.notEnabled: Content Governance is not enabled on this site, or you are not a site administrator. Enable the module in Site Settings, Modules.
settings.readOnly: Only a site administrator can change these settings.
settings.error: The settings could not be saved. Try again; if it persists, check that you are still a site administrator.
settings.loadError: The settings could not be read. Reload the page to try again.
settings.saved: Editors see the change the next time they open the drawer.
settings.intro: Choose what editors of this site find in the Content governance drawer. A section switched off also switches its site dashboard off (the entry stays and says so), and the server refuses its calls. Tabs keep their own setting while their section is off.

sectionHelp.audit: Accessibility, SEO, Web Vitals, readability, eco-design, links and Jahia checks of the page, measured in the browser, with an AI review on demand.
sectionHelp.geo: Whether AI crawlers can read the page, the site files (robots.txt, llms.txt), structured data and AI citations from BotRank. Also the GEO readiness dashboard under Additional, SEO.
sectionHelp.compliance: Terms from the site glossaries that the page and what it shows may not use, per language. Also the Compliance dashboard under Additional.

ai.title: Model shared by the AI features
ai.howTo: Until a provider, a model and a key are set, every AI feature is shown greyed out and nothing leaves the server. Only a server administrator can set them.
ai.uses: Used by the AI review tab, the SEO, alt text and plain-language assists, and the written report of the GEO readiness dashboard. The key is never sent to the browser.
